sampling_model.design: Population equality of full positive-definite covariance models is the identification kernel; the statistical rung uses independent Gaussian sampling and global BIC over the finite labelled state class.
sampling_model.units: Each observation is one independent realization of the \(p\)-variable centered linear Gaussian SEM.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment in the structure-identification theorem; the prespecified pairs in \(\mathcal Q\) index downstream interventions and responses.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; every innovation variance is positive and otherwise unrestricted.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For each candidate state and positive-definite sample covariance, target-local block-incidence matrices define positive-definite Gram systems whose unique solutions estimate the common coefficient in each parent block; strictly positive constrained residual variances estimate the innovation variances. The effect maps apply these same off-model block-constrained solutions before taking finite path sums and derivatives. A deterministic measurable fallback invokes no Gram inverse, likelihood supremum, or derivative when \(S_n\) is singular, and all asymptotic claims run through integers \(n\geq p\).

Theorem 2 transforms any pair of equivalent DAGs through exactly their distinct disagreeing edges, each reversed while covered.
Theorem 4.1 characterizes partial-homoscedastic model equivalence by ordinary Markov equivalence and fixed parent sets for vertices in nonsingleton variance blocks.
Theorem 4.4 characterizes existence and uniqueness of the MLE in a fixed compatibly coloured RDAG through augmented-sample linear independence.
The essential graph uniquely represents each ordinary DAG Markov-equivalence class and has chordal chain components.
The paper gives polynomial-time counting and uniform sampling for ordinary Markov equivalence classes by clique-picking on chordal components.

The paper establishes BIC-type asymptotic model choice for finitely many smoothly curved submodels of an exponential family.

body.tldr: Equal incoming coefficients encode communities of direct causes. The published blocked edge-coloured class permits singleton blocks, whereas BPEC is its proper no-singleton subclass and is structurally identifiable. On the full singleton-permitting blocked class, equality of the full positive-definite covariance models is characterized exactly by common skeleton and unshielded colliders, common repeated parent blocks, and fixed orientation across unequal endpoint block families; equivalently, the states are connected by partition-compatible singleton covered reversals. The static class is also the set of consistent extensions of the ordinary CPDAG after inserting the background arrows \(F(C)\), with one canonical partition lift per extension. This yields exact-once enumeration after \(O(p^3)\) initialization and \(O(p+m)\) delay, a sharp \(p!\) component bound, generic fixed-\(p\) BIC component recovery, and simultaneous inference for the finite effect set. Deterministic output-sensitive quotienting by global rational identity of compact effect circuits remains open.

project_justification.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 proves BPEC structural identifiability only after forbidding singleton edge-colour classes and explicitly leaves graphical and transformational edge-coloured equivalence open. Ordinary covered reversals ignore coefficient partitions, while partial homoscedasticity constrains innovation variances rather than incoming coefficients.
project_justification.niche: Target-local blocked colourings with unrestricted positive noise variances form a natural intermediate class: repeated blocks reveal stable causal communities, but singleton blocks retain exactly the ordinary orientation ambiguity compatible with those communities.
project_justification.fill: The project recovers repeated blocks from the identity tangent space, proves by an exact sparse regression separator that any reversed edge must join equal endpoint families, and combines these facts with monotone covered reversals to obtain the full static and transformational characterization. It then converts the static class to a canonical background PDAG: every repeated-block arrow is in \(F(C)\), every consistent extension has a unique path-independent partition lift, and the published linear-delay PDAG enumeration algorithm therefore enumerates the blocked component exactly once. The same quotient supports generic fixed-dimensional BIC recovery and simultaneous possible-effect inference, while exact output-sensitive rational-functional quotienting is isolated as a separate arithmetic-circuit problem.

body.related_work: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 is the writing and primary method anchor. Its Definition 5.14 defines blocked edge colourings without excluding singleton classes; properness is a separate condition, and BPEC is the blocked, proper no-singleton subclass. Its Theorem 5.17 proves structural identifiability within BPEC, while Question 5.19 asks for a graphical characterization of edge-coloured model equivalence. The present result agrees with that boundary on the BPEC subclass and gives a complete equivalence characterization on the published blocked superclass; it does not transfer a BPEC converse to arbitrary cross-target colourings. Chickering1995 supplies the disagreement-decreasing sequence of distinct covered reversals, while the tangent and separator arguments prove those reversals are legal for the coefficient partitions. WienobstLuttermannBannachLiskiewicz2023, Theorem 5, is used directly after forming the CPDAG-plus-\(F(C)\) PDAG: cubic Meek-closure initialization and linear-delay enumeration of consistent extensions carry over through the newly proved canonical partition-lift bijection. WienobstBannachLiskiewicz2023 addresses counting and sampling ordinary Markov classes, not rational effect-map quotienting. WuDrton2023 constrains innovation variances rather than incoming coefficients, and MakamReichenbachSeigal2023 studies likelihood geometry for a fixed compatibly coloured graph. Haughton1988 informs the finite smooth-model BIC argument. MaathuisKalischBuhlmann2009, ChangGuoMalinsky2026, and GuoPerkovic2022EfficientLS inform possible-effect estimation and inference but do not provide simultaneous inference over this full-model-equivalence component.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The population component \(\mathcal R(C)\) is an equivalence class of complete covariance-model images, not the pointwise fibre of every state fitting one exceptional covariance. Zero edges and coincident coefficients can create additional pointwise representations outside the component. The fixed directed set \(F(C)\) records orientations forced directly by unequal nonsingleton families, while ordinary collider, acyclicity, and Meek-closure constraints can compel further arrows; neither kind of compelled arrow alone identifies a numerical coefficient. Canonical PDAG enumeration is linear-delay in state outputs, but the number of distinct rational effect maps can be much smaller than the number of states. Exact global rational identity is decidable by denominator clearing and coefficient expansion, yet no deterministic output-polynomial or polynomial-delay canonicalization bound for compact arithmetic circuits is claimed.
body.honest_scope: The equivalence theorem concerns finite labelled causally sufficient linear Gaussian DAGs, target-local coefficient blocks, unrestricted real block coefficients, unrestricted positive target-specific innovation variances, and full positive-definite covariance images. It does not cover cross-target edge colours, vertex-coloured innovation variances, latent confounding, selection, cycles, or pointwise supermodel fibres. State enumeration uses the canonical CPDAG-plus-\(F(C)\) PDAG and has \(O(p^3)\) initialization and \(O(p+m)\) delay after output-linear partition lifting; attaching a shortest legal-reversal certificate has the safe bound \(O(p^5)\) per output. The sharp state-count bound is \(p!\), attained by the complete all-singleton state. Exact quotienting of the emitted compact rational effect circuits is finite but not shown output-polynomial. The BIC and confidence results remain fixed-\(p\), pointwise, and generic away from a proper algebraic exceptional set; no greedy-search consistency or uniform inference near model intersections is asserted.
body.interpretation: Repeated coefficient blocks do two jobs. They survive every observationally equivalent representation, and each of their arrows becomes background knowledge because a parent contained in a repeated block cannot have the same block family as the target. After those arrows are fixed, the remaining graph uncertainty is precisely an ordinary Markov-equivalence extension problem, and the endpoint parent sets determine all residual singleton blocks uniquely. This orientation information is structural: an arrow compelled by the PDAG or by \(F(C)\) does not by itself identify its numerical coefficient.
